items.text: Antonio (Toni) Vidal-Puig is Professor of Molecular Nutrition and Metabolism at the University of Cambridge, a position he has held since October 2009. He is Associate Director of the MRC Metabolic Disease Unit, an MRC Investigator, Lead of Cardiometabolic Medicine at the Cambridge Heart and Lung Research Institute, Honorary Consultant in Metabolic Medicine at Addenbrooke’s Hospital, and Scientific Director of the Cambridge Phenomics Centre.
items.text_zh: Antonio（Toni）Vidal-Puig 自 2009 年 10 月起担任剑桥大学分子营养与代谢学教授。他还担任 MRC 代谢疾病研究部副主任、MRC 研究员、剑桥心肺研究所心脏代谢医学负责人、Addenbrooke’s 医院代谢医学荣誉顾问医师及剑桥表型组学中心科学主任。

items.text: He obtained his medical degree at the University of Valencia in 1986 and his PhD at the University of Granada in 1992. After clinical training in Granada and research appointments at Harvard Medical School, he joined Cambridge as a Senior Research Associate in 1999. He became Lecturer in 2003 and Reader in 2006 before his appointment as Professor.
items.text_zh: 他于 1986 年获得瓦伦西亚大学医学学位，1992 年获得格拉纳达大学博士学位。在格拉纳达接受临床培训、在哈佛医学院从事研究后，他于 1999 年加入剑桥，担任高级研究员，2003 年任讲师，2006 年任 Reader，随后晋升教授。

items.text: His research elucidates the molecular mechanisms linking obesity with insulin resistance, diabetes and cardiometabolic complications, and develops related therapeutic strategies. The laboratory combines hypothesis-driven research with unbiased systems approaches, using animal models, stem cell biology, human biological samples (including induced pluripotent stem cells), advanced omics technologies and bioinformatics integration.
items.text_zh: 他的研究解析肥胖与胰岛素抵抗、糖尿病及心脏代谢并发症之间的分子联系，并探索相关治疗策略。实验室结合假说驱动研究与无偏的系统研究方法，运用动物模型、干细胞生物学、人体生物样本（包括诱导多能干细胞）、先进组学技术及生物信息学整合分析。

items.text: His contributions include the adipose tissue expandability hypothesis and the concept of lipotoxicity; energy-dissipating strategies involving mitochondrial biogenesis, mitochondrial uncoupling and brown fat differentiation and activation; hypothalamic lipid metabolism and the roles of thyroid hormone and BMP8b in energy homeostasis and brown fat activation; and systems biology and stem cell approaches to lipid networks in cardiometabolic disease.
items.text_zh: 他的科学贡献包括脂肪组织扩增能力假说与脂毒性概念；通过线粒体生物发生、线粒体解偶联及棕色脂肪分化与激活促进能量消耗的策略；下丘脑脂质代谢以及甲状腺激素、BMP8b 在能量稳态和棕色脂肪激活中的作用；以及利用系统生物学和干细胞方法研究心脏代谢疾病中的脂质网络。

items.text: My research focuses on the physiological and molecular mechanisms of metabolic syndrome, a highly prevalent condition encompassing several disorders including obesity, MASLD, diabetes and cardiovascular complications. My current projects specifically explore the role of macrophages, key immune cells involved in the progression of metabolic syndrome. These cells contribute to various aspects of disease pathogenesis, such as inflammation, fibrosis, metabolic dysregulation, and tissue regeneration. I am investigating how macrophages sense excess lipids, how they adapt metabolically, and how these processes might be targeted through therapeutic interventions to treat metabolic syndrome.

items.text: I studied Biochemistry and Biomedical Sciences (2014-2018) at the University of Valencia, where I also completed my PhD (FPU-funded, 2019-2024). During my doctoral studies, I undertook an EMBO-supported internship at the University of Cambridge (2022). My PhD thesis investigated the effects of various treatments on mouse models of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). This study revealed common patterns among these drugs, contributing to a better understanding of their mechanisms of action and identifying potential therapeutic targets and biomarkers for the disease. In 2024, I joined Professor Antonio Vidal-Puig's laboratory (TVP's lab) at the Institute of Metabolic Sciences as a research associate, a position I still hold today.

items.text: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) represents the inflammatory variant of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), characterised by steatosis and hepatocellular damage. This condition involves the activation of liver-resident macrophages (Kupffer cells) and the recruiting of monocyte-derived macrophages, which exacerbate inflammation through the secretion of inflammatory cytokines. The intrinsic lipid metabolism of macrophages is critical in determining their inflammatory status. However, the impact of alterations in lipid metabolism across different macrophage subsets within the context of fatty liver diseases remains poorly understood. Considering these observations, we aim to investigate the lipid metabolism of macrophages, focusing on membrane lipid remodelling and de novo lipogenesis across various macrophage phenotypes in MASLD and its progression to MASH. Our project will integrate data from MASLD/MASH human liver biopsies analyses and liver tissues from mouse models. This comprehensive approach aims to shed light on the potential transition from MASL to MASH. This project will address a critical gap in understanding liver disease progression, with significant implications for public health.

items.text_zh: 代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝炎（MASH）是代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝病（MASLD）的炎症性类型，以肝脂肪变性和肝细胞损伤为特征。这一过程涉及肝驻留巨噬细胞（Kupffer 细胞）的激活，以及单核细胞来源巨噬细胞的募集；它们通过分泌炎症细胞因子加剧炎症。巨噬细胞内在的脂质代谢对其炎症状态具有重要影响，但在脂肪性肝病中，不同巨噬细胞亚群的脂质代谢改变会产生怎样的影响，仍不清楚。基于这些认识，我们将研究 MASLD 及其向 MASH 进展过程中不同巨噬细胞表型的脂质代谢，重点关注细胞膜脂质重塑和从头脂肪生成。项目将整合 MASLD／MASH 患者肝活检分析数据与小鼠模型肝组织数据，以全面理解从 MASL 向 MASH 的潜在转变。这项研究将填补对肝病进展机制认识的重要空白，并具有公共卫生意义。

items.text: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) is particularly relevant due to its capacity to perform non-shivering thermogenesis through the oxidation of nutrients. items.text: BAT activation is sustained by the recruitment of progenitor cells, their activation and a permissive/enabling extracellular matrix (ECM). Hyperplastic changes in BAT require adequate ECM remodelling. Recent publications and preliminary data suggest that ECM remodelling is a relevant process for BAT activation. Also, defects in ECM remodelling, as occurs in obesity and ageing, may contribute to BAT atrophy.

items.text: My research has focused mainly on mouse studies clarifying how our body handles multi-tissue interplay, such as brain-liver-pancreas-adipose tissue-muscle-gut axis for maintaining glucose- and energy-homeostasis, and how it is dysregulated under pathophysiological conditions, such as obesity and diabetes mellitus. These crosstalk among tissues would be mediated by some metabolites including fatty acids, lipids and hormones secreted by tissue, or through sympathetic nervous system. My aim is to search for such metabolites and to clarify their physiological importance. In addition, I would like to pursuit their molecular mechanism at the cellular level using in vitro approaches.

items.text_zh: 我的研究主要通过小鼠实验，阐明身体如何协调多组织之间的相互作用，例如脑—肝—胰腺—脂肪组织—肌肉—肠道轴，以维持葡萄糖与能量稳态，以及这些过程如何在肥胖和糖尿病等病理生理状态下失调。组织间的交流可能由脂肪酸、脂质、组织分泌的激素等代谢物介导，也可能通过交感神经系统进行。我的目标是寻找这些代谢物，阐明其生理学意义，并进一步通过体外实验在细胞层面探索相关分子机制。
